sections.html:
Nelson County lists real estate at $0.56 per $100 of assessed value, billed twice a year. The spring bill goes out May 1 and is due June 5. The fall bill goes out October 1 and is due December 5. The county finished a general reassessment effective January 1, 2026, so ask the Commissioner of the Revenue which rate applies to the bill in your hand.

Tax or billRate or date
Real estate$0.56 per $100
Personal property$2.79 per $100
Machinery and tools$1.25 per $100
Spring billMailed May 1, due June 5
Fall billMailed October 1, due December 5

You can pay real estate and personal property tax online through officialpayments.com. Have your bill number, your tax map number and a credit card ready. A convenience fee applies, and it varies with the amount you pay.

Nelson County follows the usual Virginia split. The Commissioner of the Revenue assesses property, and the county Treasurer collects the tax. Questions about value go to one office and questions about a payoff go to the other.

  • Commissioner of the Revenue: 84 Courthouse Square, P.O. Box 246, Lovingston, VA 22949, phone 434-263-7070.
  • County Administrator, which also schedules the Board of Equalization: 84 Courthouse Square, phone 434-263-7000. The Board's appointment line is 434-263-7003.
  • Reassessment office: 800-213-7314, staffed by the appraisal firm the county hired.

Lovingston is the county seat. Before a closing, ask the Clerk of the Circuit Court's office about recording fees and forms.

Every property in the county was reassessed effective January 1, 2026, and Nelson County is on a four year cycle. The county hired an outside appraisal firm and worked with the Commissioner's office. The cycle follows Va. Code 58.1-3252, which sets general reassessments at every four years, or every three by board vote, and lets counties with 50,000 or fewer residents choose five or six year intervals.

Assessors visited in person, carried photo IDs and put magnetic signs on their vehicles. They took exterior photos and measurements. A value built from the outside of a house cannot see the inside, so if your interior is damaged or unfinished, ask the county what it has on file for your parcel and bring photos and repair estimates.

sections.h2: Appealing to the Board of Equalization
sections.html:
The Board of Equalization hears complaints that an assessment is unequal or above fair market value. It can raise, lower or affirm the value. The legal basis is Va. Code 58.1-3378 and 58.1-3379.

  • Timing: the 2026 session ran eight hearing days in March at the Bridge Conference Room of the Lovingston courthouse, and applications closed in April 2026.
  • Appointments: hearings are booked every 30 minutes by calling 434-263-7003.
  • Burden: you must overcome a clear presumption in favor of the assessment, using a preponderance of evidence that the value is not uniform or is above market.

Those dates belong to the 2026 cycle and are over. For a later year, the county advertises a notice with the dates that apply, and extra dates are added when needed. Call the appointment line to ask when the next session is scheduled.

Nelson County sits in central Virginia, with the Blue Ridge Mountains along the northwest and the James River along the southeast. The 2020 population was 14,775, with a 2025 estimate of 14,920. No city or incorporated town lies inside the county. Nellysford is the largest community and Lovingston is the seat, and Wintergreen, Afton, Arrington, Schuyler and Shipman are other named places.

Hurricane Camille hit the county on the night of August 19 to 20, 1969, with flash floods and mudslides. The Tye, Piney, Buffalo and Rockfish rivers all drain to the James, and creek valleys can fill quickly. If your house is near a stream, gather any flood or drainage paperwork before you list, because buyers will ask. Confirm a parcel's flood status with the county or the FEMA map before you describe it to anyone.

The county is rural. Of 9,871 housing units at the 2020 census, 34.5 percent were vacant, and among occupied homes 78.7 percent were owner occupied. Many properties are second homes or rentals, which is typical near a resort.

Wintergreen Resort, wineries, breweries, Crabtree Falls and the Blue Ridge Parkway draw visitors. A property here can be a mountain house, a farm parcel or a family home, and each raises different tax and access questions. Land with a long driveway, a well or a septic system needs those details written down before a buyer asks.

Under Va. Code 58.1-3340, taxes assessed on real estate carry a lien ahead of any other lien. The buyer, or the trustee at a foreclosure, must apply sale proceeds to those taxes, penalties and interest included, and the treasurer releases the lien afterward. If you are selling only part of a larger tract, the code prorates the tax by the share of the price, and the commissioner can ask for an appraisal when the price looks low.

In practice, selling five acres off a farm means the taxes on the whole tract enter the closing math. Your liability for the current year is prorated by the contract, so write that into the sale agreement.

Va. Code 58.1-802 adds a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500. The seller pays it unless the parties agree otherwise, and the clerk of court collects it when the deed is recorded.

Start with the Treasurer: ask for a written payoff showing every open bill. Then call the Commissioner of the Revenue if you think the 2026 value is wrong. Tell your title company about any lien or unpaid bill so nothing surprises you at the table. Bring your tax map number and the most recent bill to every call, because both offices will look up your parcel with them.

  • Ask which half of the year is already paid, and confirm whether the June 5 or December 5 bill is still open.
  • Collect flood, drainage and survey papers if the land touches a creek.
  • Check with the Clerk of the Circuit Court on recording fees.
  • If part of a tract is being sold, ask the commissioner how the share of the price will be used to split the tax.
  • Book a call early, since the office is small and the Board's appointment line fills up after a reassessment.

A cash sale skips the repairs, showings and lender appraisal, and the tax balance still comes out of the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Nelson County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The county lists $0.56 per $100 of assessed value for real estate. A general reassessment took effect January 1, 2026, so confirm the rate on your current bill with the Commissioner of the Revenue.

faqs.q: When are Nelson County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due twice a year. The spring bill is mailed May 1 and due June 5, and the fall bill is mailed October 1 and due December 5.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Nelson County assessment?
faqs.a: The Commissioner of the Revenue at 84 Courthouse Square in Lovingston handles assessments, phone 434-263-7070.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Nelson County reassessment?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Board of Equalization. The 2026 session is over, so call 434-263-7003 to ask when the next one is scheduled and how to apply.

faqs.q: Can I sell Nelson County land with taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia's tax lien is paid from the sale proceeds, and for part of a tract the tax is prorated across the whole tract by price. Ask the treasurer for a payoff before closing.
